text:
ConocoPhillips dropped 2.25% today after oil prices fell on renewed hopes for a diplomatic end to the Iran conflict. On October 27th, Iran's supreme leader and top security official discussed conditions to cease the war, and Saudi Arabia's defense minister visited Tehran to de-escalate tensions—both moves pushed crude lower. With US oil at $107.89 and world oil at $115.22, the pullback reflects reduced geopolitical risk premium that had been supporting energy prices.

The stock had climbed sharply just the day before (up to $151.37 on October 26th) as investors bet on prolonged conflict and sustained oil demand, but the diplomatic signals reversed that momentum. Even a potential Trump administration deal to allow more Russian diesel onto the market—announced on October 27th—didn't support prices, since analysts noted those volumes would be too small to move the needle.
